issues.description: Monkey-patching genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE at import time is hostile
issues.detail: Reaching into a third-party library's underscore-prefixed module to mutate a module-level constant at import time is the exact kind of cleverness that bites the maintainer in eight months when google-genai reorganizes. The comment literally says 'Temporary hack.' Temporary hacks in import blocks become permanent. Either upstream a fix, pass the buffer size through a documented API, or stream the response properly. Not this.

issues.description: image.tobytes() with format='RGB' will produce broken images for most PNGs
issues.detail: PIL's Image.open returns whatever mode the source is (RGBA, P, L, etc.). Calling .tobytes() without converting first and then declaring format='RGB' downstream means the byte layout won't match the declared format whenever Gemini returns anything other than a pure RGB image. Call image.convert('RGB') before tobytes(), or honor the actual mode. This is a correctness bug, not a style nit.

issues.description: THREE-PATCHES: feature, default-model change, and dep bumps bundled together
issues.detail: This commit does three unrelated things: adds image-generation handling, changes the default model from gemini-2.0-flash to gemini-2.5-flash (a user-visible behavior change for every existing caller), and widens three google-* dependency specifiers from ~= to >=,<3. When something regresses, bisect lands on a commit that did all three. Split them.

issues.description: Default model change is a silent breaking behavior change with no migration note
issues.detail: Flipping the default from gemini-2.0-flash to gemini-2.5-flash changes cost, latency, and output for every caller who relied on the default. The CHANGELOG entry is a one-liner under 'Changed.' Users who pinned nothing get a different model on next pip install. At minimum this deserves a louder note; arguably it should be its own PR with a deprecation cycle.

issues.description: No test, no failing-then-passing demonstration, just an example script
issues.detail: The patch claims image generation works. There is no unit test for the new inline_data branch in _process_context, no test that _maybe_unset_thinking_budget skips when 'image' is in the model name, nothing. An example file that requires a real Google API key and a webrtc transport is not a regression suite. Prose in the commit message is not the arbiter; the machine is.

issues.description: Brittle 'image' substring check for model classification
issues.detail: if 'image' in self._model_name is the kind of special case that ages badly. Tomorrow Google ships gemini-3-flash-image-preview or gemini-imagen-something and the heuristic either holds by luck or quietly breaks thinking-budget logic. A small explicit set or a documented model-capability lookup would eliminate the special case instead of accumulating more.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The actual feature — handling inline_data parts from Gemini and pushing OutputImageRawFrame — is roughly the right shape and reasonably small. But the patch ships a monkey-patch into google-genai's private _api_client at module import, an image.tobytes() call that doesn't convert mode and will produce garbled pixels for non-RGB returns, and bundles a silent default-model change plus three dependency bumps into the same diff. This is three patches submitted as one, with no tests, and one genuine correctness bug. Split it, fix the RGB conversion, and find a non-hack solution for the buffer size before this lands.
